slides.exit: Reads a simple instruction and carries it out.

sessions.teacherNote: Following instructions proves comprehension through action. Keep verbs concrete and doable in the room.
sessions.homePractice: Read one instruction at home (a label, a note) and follow it.

sessions.title: Signs and labels
sessions.goal: Today I can read short signs and labels around me.

slides.goal: Words are everywhere — on doors, shelves and bottles. We read them fast.
slides.warmup: Name one sign or label you saw today. Signs use short, useful words.

slides.oral: This bottle says milk. This tap says water. Short words help us every day.

slides.intro: Read each sign or label.

slides.title: Listen and find
slides.intro: Say a word — the learner points to the sign.

slides.title: Where would you see it?
slides.task: Read each one. Where might you see it — a shop, a bottle, a door?
slides.exit: Reads short signs and labels and says where each appears.

sessions.teacherNote: Environmental print: single words in the real world. Connect each to a place the learner knows.
sessions.homePractice: Read one sign or label you pass every day.

sessions.title: A short message
sessions.goal: Today I can read a short note and find what it says.

slides.goal: A message is a few short lines. We read to find the important parts.
slides.warmup: Have you had a text or note today? A message tells us something quickly.

slides.oral: Hi. I am at work. Get milk and bread. This is a short message from home.

slides.intro: Read this note from home.

slides.title: Listen and find
slides.intro: Say a word from the note — the learner points to the picture.

slides.title: What does it say?
slides.task: Read the message. What must you get? When will you meet?
slides.exit: Reads a short message and finds the key facts.

sessions.teacherNote: Real texts: a note has a purpose. Ask what it wants the reader to do.
sessions.homePractice: Read a real note or text message and say what it asks.

sessions.title: Tell it back
sessions.goal: Today I can read a few sentences and tell them back.

slides.goal: After we read, we can say it again in our own words.
slides.warmup: Tell me one thing about your day. Telling it back is what good readers do.

slides.oral: I have a dog. The dog likes a ball. We will read it, then tell it back.

slides.intro: Read about the dog.

slides.title: Tell it back
slides.task: Cover the text. Tell it back in your own words: what do I have? what does it like?
slides.exit: Retells a short text from memory.

sessions.teacherNote: Retelling shows the learner built meaning, not just sounded out words. Accept their own wording.
sessions.homePractice: Read three sentences, then tell someone what they said.

sessions.title: A longer text
sessions.goal: Today I can read five sentences that go together.

slides.goal: More sentences, one story. We read from the top to the end.
slides.warmup: Say two things you do in a normal day. We will read five sentences about a day.

slides.oral: The sun is up. I make tea. I go to work. Five short sentences, one day.

slides.intro: Read my morning.

sentences.text: I go to work on the **bus**.

slides.title: Listen and find
slides.intro: Say a word — the learner points to the picture.

slides.title: Answer about it
slides.task: Read all five sentences. What do I do in the morning? What do I do at night?
slides.exit: Reads a five-sentence text and answers questions about it.

sessions.teacherNote: First connected text. Track line by line; check the learner holds meaning across sentences.
sessions.homePractice: Read a short paragraph and tell one thing that happened.

sessions.title: Reading checkpoint
sessions.goal: Today I can show what I can read on my own.

slides.goal: Show all your reading: words, sentences and meaning — on your own.
slides.warmup: You have read words, sentences and short texts. Today you show it by yourself.

slides.oral: The cat is on the bed. I go to work on the bus. Read each one on your own today.

slides.intro: Read each sentence on your own.

sentences.text: I go to work on the **bus**.

slides.sentence: The cat is on the bed.

slides.title: Show what you can do
slides.task: Read each sentence with no help. Then answer: Where is the cat? How do I go to work?
slides.exit: Reads simple sentences independently and answers about them.

sessions.teacherNote: Checkpoint: minimal support. Note which skills are secure (decoding, meaning) and which need more work.
sessions.homePractice: Read three sentences to a family member with no help.

sessions.title: Signs on doors
sessions.goal: Today I can read the signs on doors.

slides.goal: Doors tell us what to do: push or pull, open or closed.
slides.warmup: Think of a shop door you use. Does it say push or pull? We will read door signs.

slides.oral: Some doors say PUSH. Some say PULL. A shop can be OPEN or CLOSED. We read the sign first.

slides.intro: These are on doors. Read each one.
More door signs.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Say what each sign means. At a door that says PULL, what do you do?
slides.exit: Reads door signs and acts on them (push/pull, open/closed).

sessions.teacherNote: Environmental print with a clear action. Mime push/pull so meaning is physical, not just decoded.
sessions.homePractice: Read the sign on one door before you open it today.

sessions.title: Safety and warning signs
sessions.goal: Today I can read signs that keep me safe.

slides.goal: Some signs keep us safe. We must read and obey them.
slides.warmup: Have you seen a red STOP sign? Red often means stop or danger.

slides.oral: STOP means stop. DANGER means keep away. NO ENTRY means do not go in. FIRE EXIT is the way out in a fire.

slides.intro: Safety signs. Read each one.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Which signs mean 'do not go'? Which one shows the way out in a fire?
slides.exit: Reads safety signs and knows which mean danger or the way out.

sessions.teacherNote: High-stakes signs. Colour is a strong cue (red=stop/danger, green=go/exit) — teach it explicitly.
sessions.homePractice: Point out one safety sign you see this week and say what it means.

sessions.title: Signs around town
sessions.goal: Today I can read signs in shops and the street.

slides.goal: Signs help us find our way in town.
slides.warmup: When you need the toilet in a shop, what sign do you look for? We will read town signs.

slides.oral: TOILETS shows where the toilet is. EXIT is the way out. LIFT takes you up and down. NO SMOKING means do not smoke.

slides.intro: Signs you see out and about.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: You need the way out. Which sign do you follow? You need the toilet — which sign?
slides.exit: Finds the right sign for a real need (exit, toilets).

sessions.teacherNote: Wayfinding. Tie each sign to a real need the learner has when out.
sessions.homePractice: Find the EXIT sign next time you are in a shop.

sessions.title: Money and prices
sessions.goal: Today I can read prices and money.

slides.goal: Prices tell us how much to pay. We read the number and the sign.
slides.warmup: How much is a loaf of bread near you? We will read prices with the pound sign.

slides.oral: £ means pounds. p means pence. £1 is one pound. 50p is fifty pence. £2.50 is two pounds and fifty pence.

slides.intro: Read each price.
A small shopping list with prices.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Which costs the most? You have £5 — is that enough for the milk, bread and eggs?
slides.exit: Reads prices and compares amounts of money.

sessions.teacherNote: Money is the highest-value functional reading. Use real coins/notes if you have them.
sessions.homePractice: Read one price on a shelf or a menu today.

sessions.title: The clock: o'clock
sessions.goal: Today I can read o'clock times.

slides.goal: The clock tells us the time. We start with o'clock times.
slides.warmup: What time do you get up? We will read whole hours on a clock.

slides.oral: When the long hand points to 12, it is an o'clock time. The short hand shows the hour.

slides.intro: Read each clock.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Say each time. Which clock shows nine o'clock? Point to it.
slides.exit: Reads whole-hour (o'clock) times on a clock face.

sessions.teacherNote: Start with the hour hand only, long hand on 12. Say the digital time and the words together.
sessions.homePractice: Look at a clock at home and say the o'clock time.

sessions.title: The clock: half past
sessions.goal: Today I can read half past times.

slides.goal: When the long hand points to 6, it is half past.
slides.warmup: You have read o'clock times. Now we read half past — the long hand on 6.

slides.oral: The long hand on 6 means half past. Half past seven is 7:30. Half past one is 1:30.

slides.intro: Read each clock.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Say each time. Which clock shows half past seven?
slides.exit: Reads half-past times on a clock face.

sessions.teacherNote: Contrast with o'clock: same hours, long hand now on 6. Keep the digital :30 visible.
sessions.homePractice: Find a half past time on a clock today (something on the :30).

sessions.title: Days of the week
sessions.goal: Today I can read the days of the week.

slides.goal: There are seven days in a week. We read them in order.
slides.warmup: What day is it today? We will read all seven days of the week.

slides.oral: The week goes Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday. Then it starts again.

slides.intro: Read the days in order.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Which day is today? Point to it and say it. Which day comes after Friday?
slides.exit: Reads the days of the week and finds today.

sessions.teacherNote: Order matters. Saturday/Sunday marked as the weekend. Anchor to the learner's own week (work/rest days).
sessions.homePractice: Say the days of the week in order before the next class.

sessions.title: The calendar
sessions.goal: Today I can read a calendar and find a date.

slides.goal: A calendar shows the days of a month. We find the right date.
slides.warmup: When is your next appointment or a family day? We will find a date on a calendar.

slides.oral: This is one month: September. Each box is a day. We find a date and point to it.

slides.intro: Look at the month. The party is on the coloured day.
slides.note: The party is on **15 September**. Find it on the calendar.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Point to 15 September. What day of the week is it? Find day 1 of the month.
slides.exit: Finds a given date on a calendar and reads the weekday.

sessions.teacherNote: One month at a time. Point to the date, then read across to the weekday header.
sessions.homePractice: Find today's date on any calendar at home.

sessions.title: An appointment card
sessions.goal: Today I can read an appointment card.

slides.goal: An appointment card tells us where and when to go.
slides.warmup: Have you had a card from a doctor or dentist? We will read one.

slides.oral: An appointment card has a name, a date, a time and a place. We read each part.

slides.intro: Read the appointment card.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: When is the appointment — the date and the time? Where must Sara go?
slides.exit: Reads the date, time and place from an appointment card.

sessions.teacherNote: Bring together date + time + place. Have the learner find each field on the card.
sessions.homePractice: Read a real appointment card or letter and find the date and time.

sessions.title: A shop receipt
sessions.goal: Today I can read a receipt and find the total.

slides.goal: A receipt shows what we bought and how much we paid.
slides.warmup: Do you keep your shopping receipts? We will read one and find the total.

slides.oral: A receipt lists each thing and its price. At the bottom is the TOTAL — all of it added up.

slides.intro: Read the receipt.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: What did Sara buy? How much was the milk? What is the total?
slides.exit: Reads items and prices on a receipt and finds the total.

sessions.teacherNote: The TOTAL line is the key. Show that it equals the items added up.
sessions.homePractice: Find the total on your next receipt.

sessions.title: A food label
sessions.goal: Today I can read a food label.

slides.goal: A label tells us about the food — and when to use it.
slides.warmup: How do you know if milk is still good? A label has a use-by date.

slides.oral: A label has the name of the food and a USE BY date. After that date, do not use it.

slides.intro: Read the milk label.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: What is this? When must you use it by? Where should you keep it?
slides.exit: Reads the name and use-by date on a food label.

sessions.teacherNote: Use-by keeps food safe. Contrast today's date with the use-by date so the learner sees why it matters.
sessions.homePractice: Read the use-by date on something in your kitchen.

sessions.title: A bus timetable
sessions.goal: Today I can read a bus timetable.

slides.goal: A timetable tells us when the bus comes.
slides.warmup: Do you take a bus? We will read the times the bus comes.

slides.oral: A timetable is a list of times. We find the time we need and take that bus.

slides.intro: Read the bus times for Bus 12.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: You must be at work by 9:00. Which bus do you take — the 8:00 or the 8:30? Point to it.
slides.exit: Reads a timetable and chooses the right bus time.

sessions.teacherNote: Reading to decide, not just to decode. Give a real goal (be at work by 9) so the choice matters.
sessions.homePractice: Find one bus or train time you need this week.

sessions.title: Fill a form: your name
sessions.goal: Today I can write my name on a form.

slides.goal: Forms often ask for your name — first name and last name.
slides.warmup: What is your first name? What is your last name? We will put a name on a form.

slides.oral: A form has boxes with labels. First name goes in one box, last name in another.

slides.intro: Tap a name, then tap the box it goes in.

slides.title: Now you
slides.task: On paper, write your own first name, then your last name.
slides.exit: Writes their own first and last name in the right places.

sessions.teacherNote: Model with the example, then personalise: the learner writes their real name. Capital letters to start.
sessions.homePractice: Practise writing your full name three times at home.

sessions.title: Fill a form: your address
sessions.goal: Today I can write my address on a form.

slides.goal: Your address says where you live: number, street, town and postcode.
slides.warmup: What is the name of your street? We will put an address on a form.

slides.oral: An address has a house number, a street, a town and a postcode. Each goes in its own box.

slides.intro: Tap the answer, then tap the right box.

slides.title: Now you
slides.task: On paper, write your own house number and street.
slides.exit: Writes their own address details in the right fields.

sessions.teacherNote: Address order is fixed (number, street, town, postcode). Use the learner's real address for production.
sessions.homePractice: Write your address on paper and check each part.

sessions.title: Fill a form: personal details
sessions.goal: Today I can complete a simple personal form.

slides.goal: Many forms ask for your name, date of birth and phone number.
slides.warmup: Do you know your phone number by heart? We will complete a short form.

slides.oral: A form can ask for your full name, your date of birth, and your phone number. We fill each box.

slides.intro: Tap the answer, then tap the right box.

slides.title: Now you
slides.task: On paper, write your own name and phone number.
slides.exit: Completes a simple personal-details form with their own information.

sessions.teacherNote: These three fields appear on nearly every form. Keep a card with the learner's details for reference.
sessions.homePractice: Write your name and phone number from memory.

sessions.title: Functional checkpoint
sessions.goal: Today I can show my everyday reading and writing.

slides.goal: Show what you can do: read a sign, read the clock, and fill a form.
slides.warmup: You have read signs, prices, clocks, calendars, cards and forms. Today you show it.

slides.intro: Read this sign.
Read this clock.
Tap the answer, then tap the box.

slides.title: Show what you can do
slides.task: Read the EXIT sign and the clock on your own. Then write your own name on paper.
slides.exit: Reads a sign and a clock and writes their name independently.

sessions.teacherNote: Light-support checkpoint across the level. Note which document types are secure and which need review.
sessions.homePractice: Read one sign, one time and write your name — all on your own.

sessions.title: Project: All about me
sessions.goal: Today I can say and write who I am.

slides.goal: Bring it together: say your name, where you live and your phone number.
slides.warmup: Say your name out loud. Today we put your details together in a little project.

slides.oral: My name is Sara. I live in Leeds. This is a project about you.

slides.intro: Tap each detail, then tap the box it goes in.

slides.title: Your project
slides.task: On paper, write your name and your town. Then say: 'My name is ___. I live in ___.'
slides.exit: Says and writes their own name and town in a full sentence.

sessions.teacherNote: Capstone opener. Combine a form, a sentence frame and speaking. Use the learner's real details.
sessions.homePractice: Write your name and town, and say the two sentences to someone.

sessions.title: Project: My family
sessions.goal: Today I can tell you about my family.

slides.goal: Make a little project about your family — names, pictures and sentences.
slides.warmup: How many people are in your family? Today we make sentences about them.

slides.oral: This is my mother. This is my father. We will read and make family sentences.

slides.intro: Read about a family.

slides.title: Your project
slides.task: Say one sentence about a person in your family. Then write it: 'This is my ___.'
slides.exit: Says and writes a sentence about a family member.

sessions.teacherNote: Integrate pictures + sentence building. Let the learner substitute their own family words.
sessions.homePractice: Draw or name three family members and make a sentence for one.

sessions.title: Project: A shopping trip
sessions.goal: Today I can plan a shop and check what I paid.

slides.goal: A whole shopping trip: make a list, read the prices, check the receipt.
slides.warmup: What do you buy most often? Today we plan a small shop from start to end.

slides.oral: First a list, then the prices, then the receipt. This is a shopping project.

slides.intro: Here is the shopping list.
Read the prices in the shop.
Now check the receipt.

slides.title: Your project
slides.task: Write your own short list of three things. What is your total if each is £1?
slides.exit: Plans a short shopping list and works out a simple total.

sessions.teacherNote: Chains list → prices → receipt into one real task. Keep totals to whole pounds.
sessions.homePractice: Write a shopping list of three things before your next shop.

sessions.title: Project: Making an appointment
sessions.goal: Today I can read an appointment and say when it is.

slides.goal: Handle a real appointment: read the card, find the day and the time, and say it.
slides.warmup: Do you have any appointments soon? Today we read one from start to end.

slides.oral: An appointment has a day, a time and a place. We find them all.

slides.intro: Read the appointment card.
Find the day on the calendar.
Read the time.

slides.title: Your project
slides.task: Say when the appointment is: the day and the time. Write the date on paper.
slides.exit: Reads an appointment and says and writes the date and time.

sessions.teacherNote: Bring doc + calendar + clock together. The learner should point to each fact across the three.
sessions.homePractice: Find a real date and time on a card or letter and say it.

sessions.title: Project: My day
sessions.goal: Today I can say what I do in a day.

slides.goal: Make a project about your day: the times, the things you do, in order.
slides.warmup: What is the first thing you do in the morning? Today we tell a whole day.

slides.oral: The sun comes up. I eat. I go to work. I sleep. This is my day.

slides.intro: These are the times in my day.
Read my day, in order.

slides.title: Your project
slides.task: Say three things you do in a day, in order. Write one: 'At ___, I ___.'
slides.exit: Describes a daily routine in order, with a time.

sessions.teacherNote: Integrate clock + connected reading + speaking about self. Order words anchor the sequence.
sessions.homePractice: Tell someone three things you do each day, with a time.

sessions.title: Project: A message
sessions.goal: Today I can read a message and write a reply.

slides.goal: A real exchange: read a short message, then write a reply back.
slides.warmup: When did you last get a text? Today we read one and answer it.

slides.oral: A friend sends a short message. We read it, then we write back.

slides.intro: Read the message.

slides.title: Your project
slides.task: Write a short reply of two lines. Say 'yes' or 'no' and a time.
slides.exit: Reads a short message and writes a short reply.

sessions.teacherNote: Reading + writing in one loop. Keep the reply to two short lines the learner can manage.
sessions.homePractice: Read one message and write a one-line reply.

sessions.title: Project: Filling in a form
sessions.goal: Today I can fill in a whole form.

slides.goal: Complete a real form from top to bottom: name, address, date of birth, phone.
slides.warmup: Forms are everywhere — at the doctor, the bank, for a card. Today we fill one right through.

slides.oral: A form asks for your details, one box at a time. We fill every box.

slides.intro: Tap each detail, then tap the right box.

slides.title: Your project
slides.task: On a paper form, write your own name, address and date of birth.
slides.exit: Completes a simple registration form with their own details.

sessions.teacherNote: The full-form capstone of L6's form work. Have the learner's details on a card to copy from.
sessions.homePractice: Fill in a real form or write your details on paper.

sessions.title: Project: Getting around
sessions.goal: Today I can follow signs to get where I need to go.

slides.goal: Use signs to find your way: the exit, the toilets, the lift.
slides.warmup: When you are in a big shop, how do you find the way out? Today we follow signs.

slides.oral: Signs point the way. We read them and go the right way.

slides.intro: Read the signs you follow.
Read the directions.

slides.title: Your project
slides.task: You want the way out. Which sign do you follow? Walk to a sign in this building and read it.
slides.exit: Follows the correct signs to reach a real place.

sessions.teacherNote: Signs + short directions in a real space. If you can, walk to an actual sign together.
sessions.homePractice: Follow one sign to find the exit or toilets somewhere this week.

sessions.title: Project: Making tea
sessions.goal: Today I can read the steps and make a cup of tea.

slides.goal: Follow a recipe: read the steps in order and do them.
slides.warmup: How do you make a hot drink? Today we read the steps for a cup of tea.

slides.oral: A recipe is steps in order. First, next, last. We read and do each one.

slides.intro: Read the steps in order.

slides.title: Your project
slides.task: Put the three steps in order: first, next, last. Then say how you make tea.
slides.exit: Reads and orders the steps of a simple recipe.

sessions.teacherNote: Instructions + sequencing + speaking. Mime the steps; order the three pictures first→last.
sessions.homePractice: Say the three steps to make tea, in order.

sessions.title: Project: My story
sessions.goal: Today I can write and read a few sentences about me.

slides.goal: The big one: write a few sentences about yourself and read them out loud.
slides.warmup: You can read words, sentences and forms. Today you write your own short story — about you.

slides.oral: My name is Sara. I live in Leeds. I have a dog. This is my story.

slides.intro: Read this story about Sara.

sentences.text: I go to **work** on the bus.

slides.title: Your project
slides.task: Write three sentences about you: your name, your town, and one thing you have or do. Read them out loud.
slides.exit: Writes and reads aloud three simple sentences about themselves.

sessions.teacherNote: Capstone of the whole pathway: independent writing + reading aloud. Celebrate it — this is real literacy.
sessions.homePractice: Write three sentences about yourself and read them to someone.
